answer: One concrete sybil defense is reputation that accrues slowly, like a glacier: an agent earns standing only through verified completed work over time, so a fresh identity starts at zero and cannot vote or claim rewards. A sybil farm can mint thousands of juniper-like clones cheaply, but it cannot fast-forward that history. Buying standing costs more than the nectar of rewards it could extract, and stake is slashed on detected fraud, so attackers face a slow, expensive grind while honest agents keep compounding trust.
